findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

REPEAT- The water dispenser heads of both coffee machines are observed to be in need of cleaning. Ensure that these are cleaned daily to be clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED- Both dispensers were cleaned during the inspection by the PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities were observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There are holes observed above the handwashing sink in the kitchen where the museum has removed an ice machine and it left two holes in the wall. Ensure that these holes are either repaired or filled and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The left of the triple sink is observed to be coming off of the wall. Ensure that this is reattached and caulked to the wall and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The walk-in freezer floor is observed to be in need of cleaning. Ensure that it is cleaned and maintained cleaned by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
At present, the facility does not have a verifiable sick policy which includes the required symptoms and diagnoses. Per person-in-charge, these are likely included in the company sick policy but this is inaccessible at this time. SCDPH provided health reporting agreements have not been completed by all staff. Person-in-charge will provide a copy of internal sick policy for inspector review via email. Person-in-charge will have SCDPH health reporting agreements completed and emailed. All employees are required to be covered by a sick policy that includes specific required diagnoses and symptoms AND affirms staff acknowledgement that they MUST report those symptoms and diagnoses to the person-in-charge. A follow-up is issued for Monday January 22, 2024 to ensure compliance with this requirement. If an email is received from person-in-charge prior to this date with signed copies of employee health reporting agreements and/or sufficient sick policy, inspector will waive the follow-up. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
A written policy for vomit and diarrhea cleanup is not available at this time. The facility does possess bleach and vomit cleanup bags but no policy that can be verified at this time. Inspector is providing the facility a copy of the SCDPH norovirus cleanup policy that may be posted in the facility to satisfy this requirement. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. Ensure that the policy is available at the next routine inspection. 

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The water dispenser heads of both coffee machines have an accumulation of residue and debris present. No mold is observed at this time. Discussed with person-in-charge the need to clean these surfaces every 24-hours to prevent contamination and accumulations from occurring. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces remain cleaned and sanitized at the proper frequencies. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Soiled mop water was observed to be sitting overnight in the facility due to closure of the utility closet prior to closure of the cafe. Soiled mop water is NEVER allowed to sit in the food service facility after completion of cleaning activities and must promptly be relayed to the proper sewage system. The mop and mop bucket were dumped and removed during the inspection. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. Ensure that waste water is immediately removed from the facility after cleaning has been completed. 

5-402.13: SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a mop bucket containing soiled water to be stored in the facility with a mop sitting in the mop water. Per discussion with person-in-charge, this mop bucket was prepared the previous night. Mop and mop buckets are left sitting overnight due to closure of the utility closet before closure of the cafe. Ensure that all mops are stored in a manner that facilitates air drying and prevents contamination. Mops may be stored hanging inverted along the wall OR in the top portion of the mop bucket. Mops may never be stored in soiled water. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
